_purpose: Validation gold set for the held-out benchmark 'the Emberlink Project'. One answer per question id, written in varied, ordinary natural-language phrasing (NOT copied from score.mjs's marker vocabulary) — proving the reused, unmodified score.mjs tolerates natural phrasing on a corpus it was never tuned against. Session numbers in the T5 answers are rung-300's (corpus/rung-300/manifest.json) — score this file with `--rung 300`. Extra `_`-prefixed keys are ignored by score.mjs, which only reads the 26 declared question ids.
t1a: Wickham's redelivery pause sits at 3000 milliseconds right now — it got dropped to 1200ms for a while, but that change caused a pile-up of redeliveries and staging fell over, so it was walked back to the original value.
t1b: Bastion's session TTL is 45 minutes these days; it started at 20 minutes and got more than doubled after complaints about people getting logged out mid-session.
t1c: Coffer's ledger is holding currency at 4 decimal places right now — it bounced from 2 up to 6 for sub-cent proration, and then settled back down to 4 as a finance compromise.
t1d: Kiln's worker pool concurrency is currently set to 6 — it got bumped up to 20 temporarily to clear a backlog, and once that backlog drained it was dialed back down to where it started.
t1e: Beacon flushes its batch buffer every 45 seconds now — that's down from the original 240-second interval, and it hasn't moved since.
t2-1: Dublin. Declan's security pass flagged an unencrypted queue connection on kiln; kiln's primary worker pool was later moved to the dub-1 region; and elsewhere dub-1 is identified as Brindlemere's Dublin facility.
t2-2: Thornquist-DB0. Ingrid's bug report was against the proration step inside checkout; that step actually lives in coffer's adjustment module; and coffer is the one service in Odalys's pod that never got migrated off the old Thornquist-DB0 datastore.
t2-3: The Expansion pod. Marisol is the one whose complaints about getting logged out mid-session led to bastion's session lifetime being lengthened, and a separate note says she manages the Expansion pod.
t2-4: Beacon. Vela's duplicate-row audit was actually about "the ledger sync process," which turns out to be an old name for beacon, and a later deploy review found beacon to be the only service still pushed out by hand instead of through CI.
t3-1: There's a conflict here that's never cleared up — one update says Emberlink Pulse runs in four regions (ord-4, dub-1, nrt-2, gru-5), but a later note says only three (ord-4, dub-1, nrt-2). Both figures are stated in the record and nothing ever says which one is right.
t3-2: Two different headcounts show up for Ingrid's QA team and neither is ever corrected: one session says six people, another says it's just five. I can't tell you which is accurate — they disagree with each other.
t3-3: The billing model is inconsistent in the record: one note reconfirms usage-based billing as the kickoff decision, but another says it's actually a flat monthly subscription with no metering. These two accounts clash and nothing in the record settles which one is current.
t3-4: Ownership of wickham is muddled — one place credits it to Odalys's Core pod, but a later note says it actually belongs to Tomasz's Platform team instead. The two don't agree and nothing ever reconciles them.
t4-1: I looked and there's no SLA uptime percentage anywhere in these sessions — sales wants a number for a contract, but no actual figure ever gets written down.
t4-2: Nothing here names a specific top customer — enterprise accounts come up in general terms a couple of times, but I never found any session that ranks or names one as the biggest by revenue.
t4-3: No programming language is ever named for wickham, or for any other service really — there's plenty of discussion of its config and its incidents, just never what it's actually written in.
t4-4: Marisol Thackeray's formal job title never shows up — she's described only by what she does (running roadmap reviews, managing the Expansion pod, raising complaints), never by a title attached to her name.
t4-5: The root cause of incident IN-4417 is never given. We know Femi got paged because kiln fell behind on its queue, and a later note says the postmortem was still waiting on one more log pull before anyone could write up why, but no session ever actually states what caused it.
t5-1: That happened right back in session 1 — that's when the project got renamed from payments-v3 to Emberlink.
t5-2: Session 6 is where Brindlemere Cloud first got picked as the hosting vendor, after the bake-off against two other finalists.
t5-3: Declan joined in session 82, introduced as the incoming security reviewer.
t5-4: The call to give trellis its own notification service instead of routing everything through wickham was made back in session 26.
t6-1: The free tier caps out at 15,000 events a month, and that number has stayed put the whole time — it comes up as the original decision, then as a support-channel reminder, then again when a prospect asked for it to be raised and got told no.
t6-2: On-call handoff happens every Wednesday morning, every two weeks, and that cadence has never budged, even though someone once floated switching to a weekly rotation.
t6-3: Staging pulls a fresh snapshot from production every Friday evening, and that schedule has been the same the whole way through.
t6-4: P1 tickets carry a six-hour response commitment, and it's held steady the entire time — a customer even asked for something faster once and was told it stays at six business hours.
